facts.statement: The only known species of Analong is Analong chuanjieensis.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Analong chuanjieensis.

facts.statement: Two giant sauropod skeletons were discovered in 1995 by Tao Wang while working with the Lufeng Dinosaur Museum.
facts.quote: The skeletons of two giant sauropods were discovered in 1995 by Tao Wang, who was working with the Lufeng Dinosaur Museum.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the village of A'na and the town of Chuanjie in Lufeng County, Yunnan.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in the village of A'na and the town of Chuanjie in the Lufeng County of Yunnan.

facts.statement: The skeletons remained in situ until 2000, when they were described and named Chuanjiesaurus.
facts.quote: They remained in situ for several years until 2000, when the two skeletons were described and given the name Chuanjiesaurus.

facts.statement: In 2020, Xin-Xin Ren and colleagues re-examined the specimen LFGT LCD9701-1.
facts.quote: In 2020, LFGT LCD9701-1 was re-examined by Xin-Xin Ren and colleagues.

facts.statement: Ren and colleagues determined that LFGT LCD9701-1 was distinct enough from the Chuanjiesaurus holotype to warrant a new genus and species, Analong chuanjiensis.
facts.quote: In this publication, Ren and colleagues determined that there were sufficient differences between LFGT LCD9701-1 and the holotype of Chuanjiesaurus were sufficient for them to erect a new genus and species to contain the specimen—Analong chuanjiensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Analong refers to the village of A'na and the suffix '-long' means 'dragon' in Mandarin.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to the village of A'na and the suffix "-long" is a transliteration of the Mandarin word for "dragon".

facts.statement: The specific epithet chuanjieensis refers to the town of Chuanjie where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific epithet refers to the town of Chuanjie, where the fossils were unearthed.

facts.statement: Ren and colleagues originally classified Analong as a basally-branching member of Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: In their initial description of Analong, Ren and colleagues found it as a basally-branching member of Mamenchisauridae.

facts.statement: Subsequent studies have reaffirmed Analong's classification as a mamenchisaurid.
facts.quote: Subsequent authors have reaffirmed its affinities as a mamenchisaurid.

facts.statement: Analong lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 168 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace 168 millones de años, durante el Batoniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Remains of Analong have been found in the Chuanjie Formation in Yunnan Province, China.
facts.quote: Sus restos se han encontrado en la Formación Chuanjie situada en la provincia de Yunnan, China.

facts.statement: Analog lived between 170.9 and 168.2 million years ago during the Bajocian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bajocian (170.9 to 168.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Analong belongs to the parent group Mamenchisauridae.
Phylogenetic analysis by its describers suggests Analong was the first mamenchisaurid to diverge evolutionarily within the group.
facts.quote: En el análisis filogenético realizado por sus descriptores, se encontró que Analong sería el mamenquisáurido que primero divergió evolutivamente dentro del grupo.

facts.statement: In 2008, an exhibition called Lufeng World Dinosaur Valley was constructed around the skeletons.
facts.quote: In 2008, the Lufeng World Dinosaur Valley exhibition was built around the skeletons.
